description: Travel editorial content for UniqueStaysUSA journal. SEO-first dispatches with affiliate stay embeds. Voice: warm, first-person, slightly literary. Think Kinfolk meets Monocle meets a dog-eared travel journal.

userStories.title: Initialize ralph and verify setup
userStories.description: Database initialized, content dirs created, PRD written
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/ralph/prd.json exists
content/drafts/ directory exists
content/published/ directory exists
scripts/ralph/progress.txt exists

userStories.title: Plan the Joshua Tree destination dispatch
userStories.description: Create a content plan for the first journal post: 'The Best Unique Stays in Joshua Tree'. Target queries: 'unique stays Joshua Tree', 'best Airbnb Joshua Tree', 'unique vacation rentals Joshua Tree CA'. Post should embed 3-5 stay cards from the directory and read as a first-person editorial dispatch.
acceptanceCriteria: Target keyword identified
Post structure outlined (opening dispatch, stay sections, closing tip)
Stay slugs to embed identified from the directory
Word count target set (1200-1800 words)
Meta title and meta description drafted
userStories.notes: Destination pillar. First post establishes the dispatch format.

userStories.title: Write first draft of Joshua Tree dispatch
userStories.description: Write the full editorial post. First-person voice. Warm, slightly literary. Not a listicle — it reads like a letter from a friend who scouted the place. Opens with scene-setting desert prose, then weaves stays into the narrative. Ends with a practical tip (best time to visit, what to pack).
acceptanceCriteria: Opening paragraph: atmospheric, sensory desert scene-setting
3-5 stay recommendations woven into the narrative
Each stay: name, 2-3 sentences of editorial description, one detail that makes it unique
Closing section: 'When to Go' practical tip
SEO keywords naturally integrated (not stuffed)
Saved to content/drafts/joshua-tree-unique-stays.md
userStories.notes: Use /elite-copywriter for the actual writing. Tone: The Paris Review meets a road trip zine.

userStories.title: Review and sharpen the Joshua Tree draft
userStories.description: Self-review the draft. Strengthen the opening. Cut any generic travel writing clichés. Make sure each stay description earns its place. Add a compelling title and subtitle. Add meta description.
acceptanceCriteria: Opening paragraph revised to be more vivid/specific
Any clichés removed ('hidden gem', 'off the beaten path', etc.)
Title: specific + searchable + editorial
Subtitle: evocative one-liner for the polaroid caption
Meta title: under 60 chars, includes 'Joshua Tree'
Meta description: under 160 chars, includes primary keyword
Version 2 saved to content/drafts/joshua-tree-unique-stays-v2.md
userStories.notes: Be brutal. Cut filler. Every sentence should earn its place.

userStories.title: Finalize and output Joshua Tree post for Payload CMS
userStories.description: Create the final publish-ready version with all fields needed to create the blog post in Payload CMS admin.
acceptanceCriteria: Final post saved to content/published/joshua-tree-unique-stays.md
Frontmatter includes: title, subtitle, slug, excerpt, city, state, latitude, longitude, metaTitle, metaDescription, publishedAt
Body is clean markdown ready for Payload's rich text editor
Stay embed markers clearly noted as [EMBED: stay-slug] placeholders
Word count: 1200-1800
userStories.notes: Output is a file Jon uses to create the post in Payload admin at /admin.
